response.justification: Broad, long-tenured engineer with genuine high-throughput distributed systems experience (millions of HTTP requests/sec at Sociomantic/dunnhumby), current Staff-level title, and hands-on exposure to agentic tooling (MCP code generators, AI-agent infrastructure) that maps directly to the AI-native environment. However, the biggest gap is the explicit must-have of strong Python — it appears nowhere in the skills list or role descriptions, with the depth instead in TypeScript/Node and DLang. Evidence of staff-scope technical strategy, cross-functional stakeholder management, and on-call/incident ownership is also thin; the resume reads as a hands-on full-stack craftsman rather than a domain technical strategist. Worth a screen to probe Python depth, scale ownership, and strategy scope, but not a clear yes on paper.
strengths: Real high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems experience at ad-tech scale
Current hands-on work with AI-agent infrastructure and MCP developer tooling
Deep engineering craft: TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development, open-source test tooling, teaching/talks
concerns: No demonstrated Python, a stated must-have for the role
Little evidence of staff-level technical strategy, org-wide influence, or stakeholder management
Operational ownership, on-call/incident response, and agile ceremony leadership are not evidenced
